solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Politician, one found behind bars after case of revenge

indicators.note: the bar-keeper comes after the revenge letters, so this orders the charade
the case of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters of revenge are kept

parts.note: a publican stands behind the bar of a pub

explanation.surface: A politician ends up in prison after a vengeful episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind bars' suggests jail, but the bars are pub bars and the person behind them runs the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A Republican is a member of the US Republican Party, an example of a politician.

clue.text: Understand refusal to cut cash crop

indicators.note: one word cuts into another, so the refusal goes inside the crop

parts.note: cotton is grown to be sold, a classic cash crop
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A farmer says no to cutting back a profitable crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refusal' and 'cut' read as a farmer's decision, but they are the insertion instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on is an informal idiom for grasping or realising something.

clue.text: Result of toned down swear word and shocking treatment

parts.note: eff is the polite stand-in for a stronger four-letter word
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, a treatment by electric shock

explanation.surface: Mild cursing and electric shocks produce an outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: An effect is the consequence or outcome of a cause.

clue.text: Notes air shot? It could be Barcelona's miss

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer misses the notes of a tune, a slip a footballer from Barcelona might make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' reads as a missed shot at goal in Barcelona, but it is a young unmarried woman there.
explanation.definitionFit: Señorita is the Spanish title for an unmarried young woman, the equivalent of Miss.

clue.text: Puts on stone over long period

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
ages is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone gains a lot of weight over a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts on stone' looks like weight gain; 'Puts on' means mounts a show. A stone is 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage a play is to put it on, i.e. present it in performance.

clue.text: Offering front of Guardian and other papers

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the i and the FT (Financial Times) are two other British newspapers

explanation.surface: A newsstand display of the Guardian next to rival papers.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British national newspaper; FT is the Financial Times, the very paper printing this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is something offered or presented to someone.

clue.text: Change decor, wanting the ultimate in chic?

definitions.text: Change decor, wanting the ultimate in chic?

indicators.note: changing the word means rearranging its letters
wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away
the ultimate letter is the last one

explanation.surface: Someone redecorates a room because it lacks the last word in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' removes C, the last letter of chic, from decor; 'Change' rearranges the remaining DEOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo a room is to redecorate it, giving it a fresh look.

clue.text: Definitely make time to go in shower

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them

indicators.note: the time letter goes into the shower word

parts.note: a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: An instruction to make the time to have a shower.
explanation.definitionFit: For certain is an idiom meaning without doubt or surely.

clue.text: Perhaps CID men also ran rum, criminally

indicators.note: done criminally means corruptly or wrongly, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Police detectives find men who smuggled rum.
explanation.walkthrough: CID looks like the British Criminal Investigation Department, but it is the number 501 in Roman figures.
explanation.definitionFit: CID is 501 written in the Latin number system, an example of these figures.

clue.text: Old lady's garment the French put on chest

indicators.note: the French article is put after the chest word

parts.note: the bust is a woman's chest
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French garment placed over an old lady's chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustle was a padded frame worn under Victorian women's skirts, a period item of clothing.

clue.text: James Bond once holding gun somewhere in London

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it

parts.note: Roger Moore played James Bond in the films
gat is old slang for a gun

explanation.surface: 007 carries a pistol on a mission in London.
explanation.walkthrough: MOORGATE is an area and station in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorgate is a district of central London, so it is a place in the capital.

clue.text: Seafood in great quantity on board

indicators.note: the quantity word is placed on after the board word

parts.note: a plank is a long board
a ton, or tons, is a great quantity

explanation.surface: Plenty of fish is loaded aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seafood' suggests a fish supper; it is food floating in the sea, eaten by whales.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are tiny drifting organisms that sea creatures feed on.

clue.text: Where dirty crockery may be picked up, working together

indicators.note: something picked up is heard, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: dirty plates may be in the sink

explanation.surface: Dishes lifted out of the sink by people washing up as a team.
explanation.definitionFit: In sync means synchronised, acting in harmony at the same time.

clue.text: Wearing filmy garment, nymphomaniac's clothing shows a lack of care

indicators.note: the inner letters wear the garment, sitting inside it

parts.note: a negligee is a light, sheer dressing gown

indicators.note: the clothing of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A seductress in a sheer nightdress is careless about cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The racy surface hides a plain container: the garment surrounds the two outer letters, placed just before its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligence is the failure to take proper care, as in law.

clue.text: Discussing eg Boris Johnson making up stories

parts.note: Boris Johnson was a Conservative prime minister, and Con is short for Conservative
to fabulate is to invent stories

explanation.surface: A jibe at a former British prime minister's habit of inventing tales.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole tail reads like one definition of a liar, but Boris Johnson only supplies CON, the abbreviation for a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: To confabulate is to chat or confer, so confabulating means talking things over.

clue.text: A bit of wind, you heard, suppressed by American ruler

indicators.note: in a down entry the first part sits under, held down by, the second
what you heard is spoken, so these words are taken by sound

parts.note: a gust is a short burst of wind
US means American

explanation.surface: An American ruler muffles a sudden breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'a gust' gives the month name AUGUST; US goes below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus was the first Roman emperor, so a historical ruler.

clue.text: Football club brought back toilet break

parts.note: Inter is Inter Milan, an Italian football club

indicators.note: brought back means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory

explanation.surface: A football club's toilet break is brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses LAV to VAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a break, as at half-time or between acts.

clue.text: Disconnect from current hype by a Parisian

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces stand side by side

parts.note: un is French for a, as said in Paris
a plug is a piece of promotional hype

explanation.surface: A Parisian unplugs from the latest hype.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' reads as up-to-date, but it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: To unplug an appliance cuts it off from the electricity supply.

clue.text: Slowly moving pieces in large shop

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large
Argos is a British chain of catalogue shops

explanation.surface: Slow-moving goods sit in a big store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slowly moving pieces' suggests stock that sells slowly; they are musical movements played slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A largo is a musical movement or piece in a slow, broad tempo.

clue.text: Great thinker seen as a mug in his homeland?

parts.note: ein is German for a, the language of the thinker's homeland
a stein is a German beer mug

explanation.surface: A genius is thought a fool back home in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' suggests a fool, but it is a drinking vessel; the thinker was born in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein is the physicist famed as a great scientific mind.

clue.text: Revolutionary article on painter in Japanese city

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece is placed on top of the second
revolutionary means turning round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Goya was a Spanish painter

explanation.surface: A revolutionary piece written about an artist in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reverses AN to NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagoya is a major city on Honshu, Japan.

clue.text: Harry Kane bagging at least four cups, in a state

indicators.note: bagging means putting into a bag, so one piece surrounds another
to harry is to harass or disturb, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: each bra has two cups, so bras plural have at least four

explanation.surface: England striker Harry Kane collects trophies and is in a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the footballer's first name but is the anagram signal; Harry Kane is an England football captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: English pan a feature of Star Wars

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese frying pan

explanation.surface: A British pan turns up in a famous science-fiction film.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewoks are the furry forest creatures who appear in Return of the Jedi.

clue.text: Government nearly burning green space

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ardent means burning with passion

explanation.surface: A government almost on fire over a green issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden is a cultivated plot of planted ground, an area of greenery.

clue.text: Head in business repeatedly timid where one has a fling?

indicators.note: repeatedly means the business abbreviation is given twice over

parts.note: co is the abbreviation for company, a business
nut is slang for the head
shy means timid

explanation.surface: A shy boss repeatedly hiding in the office, perhaps after an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fling' suggests an affair; at a fairground coconut shy you fling balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A coconut shy is a fairground stall where people throw balls to knock coconuts down.

clue.text: Knowing what soldiers do to depose leader

indicators.note: deposing the leader removes the first letter

parts.note: soldiers march

explanation.surface: Soldiers know how to march to overthrow their commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depose leader' sounds like a coup, but it removes M from MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means knowing or mischievously sly, as in an arch smile.
